references.collectionNotes: The audit was undertaken in March 2020 and May 2020. Data was collected from households in urban and rural areas as well as commercial premises. A total of 201 household samples and 47 commercial samples were gathered. In addition, around 416 landfill samples were collected and the waste composition, recycling potential, hazardous waste status and life were audited for landfills over a two-week period. The data provided for urban and rural areas is assumed to be representative of the rest of the country

references.notes: Proportions of ceramic (0.16%), aluminium (0.33%), other metal (0.33%), rubber (0.33%) and other (0.85%) waste estimated from the relative size of pie chart as they were not specified. ‘Other’ and ‘ceramic’ combined in ‘other’. The composition (%) of “generation waste” (Fig 2-5) was converted to a mass fraction of 1,060. As glass fraction was extremely high, it was assumed to include reusable bottles, which are not waste. Therefore, this mass was substituted with the mass of glass in ‘discharged waste’ (Fig 2-6), calculated as 4% of 387 g = 15.48 g. The proportions of each fraction were then recalculated as % wt.
